tasks.notes: Over-general lookup resolution in `fleet/run-waves.mjs` (`FILES_KEYS` / `makeFilesFor`). The driver supplies exactly one shape — `run-main.mjs`'s `filesFor: (opts) => ...`, a function of the dispatch object — yet the resolver accepts seven alias keys (`filesFor`, `filesOf`, `filesForLabel`, `filesForTask`, `taskFilesOf`, `taskFiles`, `files`), three argument shapes (label, id, opts), Map and plain-object specs, plus an empty/non-empty tri-state. The new exam legs hand three of those aliases in at once (`filesOf`, `filesFor`, `taskFilesOf`), so no assertion pins the name or the argument shape the production wiring actually uses — the machinery is untested surface that exists to make any wiring pass. Two concrete consequences: (1) `try { v = spec(arg) } catch { v = null }` swallows a throwing lookup, so a wiring bug degrades to "scope unknown" and silently drops every untracked binary in the clone instead of surfacing through the existing `capture:error` path; (2) the final `return sawEmpty ? [] : fromPrompt` is dead — `fromPrompt` is `[]` on that branch either way. Suggest narrowing to one documented `filesFor(opts, id, prompt)` contract plus the `FILES:`-line fallback, and letting a lookup's throw propagate into the capture's catch.; unverified: the run-main → composeAgent → withPatchCapture wiring is not exercised by the exam. Legs (a)–(d) in `fleet/tests/test_run_waves.mjs` construct `withPatchCapture` directly with their own lookup, so nothing asserts that `run-main.mjs:575-583`'s `filesByTask` (built from `argsObj.waves.flat()` with `t.files`) reaches the capture, nor that `composeAgent`'s `...(filesFor ? { filesFor } : {})` spread lands. The code reads correct — `run-main.mjs:546` already treats `argsObj.waves.flat()` entries as task objects with `.id`, and `run-engine.mjs:258` builds `filesLine` from the same `task.files` array — but a regression there (a compiled task without `files`, a renamed key) would fall through to the prompt's `FILES:` line or to an empty scope with no test failing. What would settle it: a leg composing the agent via `composeAgent` (or an assertion in `fleet/tests/test_run_main.mjs`, outside this task's Files) that a task whose FILES names a binary still carries that binary through the composed capture.; `makeFilesAllow` (`fleet/run-waves.mjs`) treats a Files entry as a directory prefix only when it ends with `/`, and matches otherwise by exact path. A plan that scopes a task to `assets` rather than `assets/` therefore has its own generated binaries under that directory dropped from the capture, with only the `capture:dropped` event to say so. Not reachable from this repo's plan shape (every Files entry is a file path), so advisory; if you want the safe reading, treat an entry with no extension that prefixes a path at a `/` boundary as a directory too.; `EVENT_KINDS` in `skills/ultralearn/scripts/fleet_events.py:24-27` enumerates the engine's emitted vocabulary (its comment cites `fleet/run-waves.mjs:215-293` as the source) and does not list the new `capture:dropped`. Nothing breaks — the comment states the set names what is known and does not filter, so the event still parses and renders — but the census vocabulary is now stale against the emitter. The fix lies outside this task's FILES (`fleet/run-engine.mjs`, `fleet/run-main.mjs`, `fleet/run-waves.mjs`, `fleet/tests/test_run_waves.mjs`), so it belongs to a follow-up, not to this diff.; Speculative generality in the new lookup resolution. `makeFilesFor` (fleet/run-waves.mjs) accepts seven key aliases (`filesFor`, `filesOf`, `filesForLabel`, `filesForTask`, `taskFilesOf`, `taskFiles`, `files`), three spec shapes (function / Map / plain object / array), three argument shapes (label, id, opts), a per-call try/catch, plus an `opts.files` fallback — while production has exactly one caller: `run-main.mjs` passes `filesFor: (opts) => ...`, and the engine's worktree dispatches (run-engine.mjs:1189 and siblings) carry no `files` key, so that branch is dead. `makeFilesAllow`, `droppedBinaryPaths` and `filesFromPrompt` are exported but imported by nothing, including the exam (fleet/tests/test_run_waves.mjs:14). The exam deliberately hands the same lookup under three of the aliases ("any one of them satisfying is a pass"), so the extra shapes are graded by nothing. Collapse to one documented shape — `filesFor(opts)` returning the task's compiled `files` array — and drop the unused exports; the Context only asks that the per-task list reach the wrapper by label.; unverified: the wrapper never passes `files: null`, so the drop is armed for every existing `withPatchCapture` caller, not only the ones that supply a lookup. `patchAgainstBase` keeps the old whole-tree behavior only when `files == null`, but `withPatchCapture` always passes `filesFor(opts, id, prompt)`, which returns `[]` (an empty allow list = drop every untracked binary) when no lookup was supplied and the prompt carries no `FILES:` line. That silently changes capture behavior for `fleet/tests/_engine_helpers.mjs:62`, `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_examiner.mjs:51`, `test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs:289`, `test_weave_emit.mjs:35` and the other harnesses that construct the wrapper without one, and for any real dispatch whose task id misses `filesByTask` (e.g. a numeric task id in the plan vs. the string `defaultTaskIdOf` returns). Acceptance is the committed suite, but the only execution evidence here is `node fleet/tests/test_run_waves.mjs`; running the rest of `fleet/tests/*.mjs` would settle it. Safer shape: have the resolver return `null` when nothing named a scope and pass that through, so an uninstrumented caller keeps the pre-task capture exactly.; The exam never exercises the "untracked at BASE" half of M1. The fixture repo tracks exactly one path at BASE2 and it is text (`app/registry.py`, asserted at the `ls-files` line), so every binary in every leg is untracked by construction: deleting the `git ls-tree` guard at the end of `droppedBinaryPaths` (`return candidates.filter((p) => !tracked.has(p)).sort()`) leaves all four legs green, while a modification to a binary tracked at BASE and outside FILES would then be silently dropped from the patch — the condition the Context spells out (`git ls-tree` at the task's base sha, never the clone's index). Add a leg: commit a binary (say `assets/tracked.bin`) into the BASE2 commit, modify it in a clone whose FILES names only `app/registry.py`, and assert it is still in `binaryPathsIn(r.patch)` and absent from the `capture:dropped` paths.; `filesFromPrompt` matches the first `^FILES:` line anywhere in the prompt, and the engine emits the task body BEFORE its own `filesLine` (run-engine.mjs:1185-1186, 1401, 1245). A task body that quotes a line starting with `FILES:` (plans in this repo routinely quote prompt fragments) would therefore be read as the task's scope by the fallback, and a binary the real FILES list names would be dropped. Since the fallback only fires when the primary lookup missed, the cheap hardening is to anchor it to the engine's line — e.g. take the LAST `^FILES:` match rather than the first, or only consult the prompt when the lookup returned nothing at all rather than when it returned empty.

completenessFindings.detail: fleet/run-engine.mjs:1718 (Task 1, adjacent to its Claim, not a shortfall of it): the reconcile path in the integration clone still stages the whole tree with `git add -A` and commits it. The candidate suite runs in that same clone, so on the operator's motivating case — a Python target with no `.gitignore` — `__pycache__/*.pyc` left by the candidate suite is committed onto the integration branch. Task 1's drop rule is deliberately capture-side only (`patchAgainstBase` in fleet/run-waves.mjs:317-334), so this channel is untouched; the Claim is about what reaches a `.patch` and about the fold not parking, and both hold, so this does not block. Related: the two "changed nothing" guards at fleet/run-engine.mjs:1727-1728 compare the staged tree against the candidate and HEAD, and regenerated bytecode alone is enough to make both differ, so a reconcile that edited no source can still be credited with a commit on such a target.
